Bash(# Check what timezone the observations use for KLGA
curl -s "https://api.weather.com/v1/location/KLGA:9:US/observations/historical.json?apiKey=e1f10a1e78da46f5b10a1e78da96f525&units=e&startDate=20260301&endDate=20260301" 2>&1 | python3 -c "
import sys, json, datetime
d = json.load\(sys.stdin\)
obs = d.get\('observations', []\)
print\('First and last observation timestamps:'\)
for o in [obs[0], obs[-1]]:
    ts = o['valid_time_gmt']
    dt = datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp\(ts, tz=datetime.timezone.utc\)
    print\(f'  UTC: {dt.isoformat\(\)} temp={o[\\"temp\\"]}'\)
    # Also show EST
    est = datetime.timezone\(datetime.timedelta\(hours=-5\)\)
    dt_est = datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp\(ts, tz=est\)
    print\(f'  EST: {dt_est.isoformat\(\)} temp={o[\\"temp\\"]}'\)
print\(\)
print\('All timestamps in EST:'\)
for o in obs:
    ts = o['valid_time_gmt']
    est = datetime.timezone\(datetime.timedelta\(hours=-5\)\)
    dt = datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp\(ts, tz=est\)
    print\(f'  {dt.strftime\(\\"%H:%M\\"\)} EST  temp={o[\\"temp\\"]}°F'\)
" 2>&1)

Bash(# Check Seoul timestamps to understand day boundaries for non-US
curl -s "https://api.weather.com/v1/location/RKSI:9:KR/observations/historical.json?apiKey=e1f10a1e78da46f5b10a1e78da96f525&units=m&startDate=20260301&endDate=20260301" 2>&1 | python3 -c "
import sys, json, datetime
d = json.load\(sys.stdin\)
obs = d.get\('observations', []\)
print\(f'Seoul RKSI March 1: {len\(obs\)} observations'\)
print\('Timestamps \(UTC / KST\):'\)
kst = datetime.timezone\(datetime.timedelta\(hours=9\)\)
for o in [obs[0], obs[-1]]:
    ts = o['valid_time_gmt']
    dt_utc = datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp\(ts, tz=datetime.timezone.utc\)
    dt_kst = datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp\(ts, tz=kst\)
    print\(f'  UTC: {dt_utc.strftime\(\\"%Y-%m-%d %H:%M\\"\)} KST: {dt_kst.strftime\(\\"%Y-%m-%d %H:%M\\"\)} temp={o[\\"temp\\"]}°C'\)
" 2>&1)
